title: Vision Zero progress and tighter fireworks rules
subtitle: Tree conservation review, Indigenous land restoration at Pioneer Tower, holding provision removals, private street names and a noise exemption.
overview: The Community and Infrastructure Services Committee recommended implementing the Vision Zero hot spot road safety improvements and received a progress update on 2022 work {{vote:m6}}. Staff said school zones are being targeted through lower speed limits, automated speed enforcement and data-driven enforcement.

The committee also recommended cutting permitted fireworks days to the day of celebration only, with displays ending by 11 pm {{vote:m7}}. Chapters 544 and 739 of the Municipal Code would be merged into a revised Chapter 739. An amendment to add Lunar New Year was defeated. The committee recommended a second phase of the tree conservation review {{vote:m8}} and a Land Restoration Project at Pioneer Tower Natural Area with Indigenous partners and Conestoga College {{vote:m9}}.

Routine items were also recommended: removing holding provisions at 2155 Strasburg Road {{vote:m1}} and 9 Cameron Street North {{vote:m2}}, two private street names, and a noise exemption for the Greek Food Festival. These are recommendations that Council will consider later.

decisions.detail: The committee received the 2022 progress update and recommended that staff implement the hot spot improvements listed in Appendix A of the report.
The committee recommended limiting fireworks displays to the day of celebration (Victoria Day, Canada Day, Diwali) ending by 11 pm, and merging Chapters 544 and 739 into a revised Chapter 739.
The committee recommended that staff start a second phase evaluating specific enhancements to existing tree conservation tools and processes.

The committee recommended proceeding with the Wiijindamaan Indigenous Land Restoration Project and authorizing the General Manager, Infrastructure Services to sign partner agreements, subject to City solicitor review.
The committee recommended approving removal of Holding Provision 29H from the lands at 2155 Strasburg Road.
The committee recommended approving removal of Holding Provision 15H from the lands at 9 Cameron Street North.
The committee recommended a Chapter 450 noise exemption for the festival at 527 Bridgeport Road East on June 10 and 11, 2023, from 12 p.m. to 11 p.m.

debate: On Vision Zero, councillors asked about school zones, police enforcement, automated speed cameras run by the Region, and roundabout lighting. Staff said the camera program and ticket processing are Regional matters. One councillor asked about cheaper, more mobile alternatives, and staff said a city-run model was costly with no offsetting revenue.

On fireworks, some councillors wanted a ban or sanctioned community sites. Staff raised insurance and liability, and a senior staff member said a review of sanctioned events could take 6 to 12 months for an already busy by-law team. Complaints are hard to enforce because fireworks end quickly and callers rarely give an address.

A proposal to add Lunar New Year to the fireworks days was opposed. Reasons given were that no community group had asked for it, as happened with Diwali, and that it could lead to requests for other holidays. Supporters cited equity and the diversity of the city.

On trees, some councillors favoured incentives and education over penalties. One stressed balance with the housing supply and noted canopy growth from 2014 to 2019. Others wanted more protection for mature trees, a policy for lots under one acre, and more street trees downtown. Staff said enforcement is hard because evidence is difficult to collect after the fact.

On the Pioneer Tower project, councillors were supportive and asked about funding, trail links and invasive species. Staff said a Conestoga College grant drives the restoration work and the City contributes in-kind support and natural areas capacity. The land is largely floodplain.
